newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly down in very slow trading on Tuesday, with investors sidelined following an overnight public holiday on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at 20,250 yuan ($2,437) per tonne, losing 30 yuan. It opened at 20,230 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,220 and a high of 20,280.
September and October did not trade. November fell 40 to 20,330 yuan, the January 1997 contract 60 to 20,200 and February 50 to 20,250.
Combined volume fell sharply to 4,695 tonnes from 16,490.
Copper opened down and moved in a very narrow range of 100 yuan for most of the session.
Traders said most investors were sidelined following a public holiday on the LME, but some profit-taking pushed prices slightly down.
"Speculators dominated today's trading, but most investors are waiting for copper's opening on the LME," one trader said.
Traders said copper's short-term trend was not clear, but it was likely to find support at 20,000 yuan.
"Copper is not likely to breach the key 20,000-yuan support level despite poor fundamentals and weak sentiment," a second trader said. "It will move between 20,000 and 20,500 in the next few days."
Aluminium ended down. September fell 130 to 14,270 yuan, October 70 to 14,180 and November 20 to 14,170.
Combined volume rose to 480 tonnes from 350.
